location: Boundaries > Always (Plan's per-cell rerun_matrix reasons) / Tasks > tests ('hand-written warm/partial/not-run records ... hide no older gate-grade record') vs cell-contract.md > Plan reason list ('then by the newest fresh record: fail, not-run, inconclusive, warm-only, partial, ...') and > Newest ('each rule below picks the newest record that matches it')
issue: The reason chain doesn't say which record is judged when a warm, partial or not-run record is newer than a fresh gate-grade record that is not passing. Take the history [cold full fail, then warm pass], both fresh. Read literally ('the newest fresh record'), the reason is `warm-only`. Read with the Newest bullet and the task's 'hide no older gate-grade record', it is `fail`. The aggregate side is fixed either way: `e2e_state` is `fail` (newest gate-grade is `fail`) and `versions[ver].reason` is the literal `fail`. So under the literal reading, `e2e_cells[ver][b].reason` would be `warm-only` while the selected record's `state` is `fail`. The same question comes up for [cold full inconclusive, newer partial pass] (`inconclusive` or `partial`?) and [gate-grade fail, newer not-run] (`fail` or `not-run`?).
implementation_impact: `cell_reason` can be written two ways that disagree, and the plan tests, aggregate tests and the operator-facing reason all depend on the choice. The task's warm/partial/not-run tests pass under either reading only if every fixture happens to have no older gate-grade record.
suggestion: Pin the rule in Design Notes > Reasons. For example: when the cell has a fresh gate-grade record, judge `fail`/`inconclusive-steps`/`not-gradeable`/`scenario-notes`/`browser-notes` on the newest gate-grade record; use `not-run`/`inconclusive`/`warm-only`/`partial` only when no fresh gate-grade record exists. Add one test row [cold full fail, warm pass] with the expected plan reason and `e2e_cells` reason.

location: Boundaries > Always (`ps-e2e-run.py` ... 'exit codes per Runner (0 only when every driven cell passes or E2E is skipped, 3 any fail, else 1)') / Design Notes > Record ('ps-run-layer computes state/conclusive/reason at merge')
issue: The child's exit code depends on per-cell `state`, but the spec puts the State rule only in ps-run-layer's merge (via `record_state` in ps-plan-layers.py). Nothing says how the child derives `pass`/`fail`: by importing ps-plan-layers (which itself lazily imports ps-e2e-run), by a second copy of the rule, or from today's `r["pass"]`. The zero-driven-cells case is also open. On a boot or install failure, when every engine is dropped by the probe, or when every engine fails to launch, 'every driven cell passes' is vacuously true, which reads as exit 0. Contract Runner says 1 for an infra failure.
implementation_impact: A second copy of the State rule can drift from ps-run-layer's. The vacuous reading would make a boot failure exit 0, so direct runs and the quickstart RED/GREEN step would read green on a dead container.
suggestion: State that the child computes each emitted cell's state with the same function ps-run-layer uses (name it, and say how it is loaded without an import cycle). Also state that exit 0 needs at least one driven cell whose state is `pass` and no cell in any other state; with zero driven cells the exit is 1.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration ('V's loop ends when ... no scoped cell of V has a `fail` record of session `<t>` on the current fingerprint'; 'infra retry: after such a run that appended no `fail` but a record with an infra cause (... e.g. missing image, `browser-unavailable`)')
issue: Both interim conditions need record-level facts that no script output in this slice exposes. The Runner output line gives only `appended` cells and `source_fingerprint`, with no per-cell state or reason. The plan's per-cell reason is the generic `inconclusive` or `fail` and does not say which session the record came from. The aggregate's `e2e_cells.reason` is also the plan reason. So the orchestrator cannot tell a `fail` of session `<t>` from an older session's `fail` on the same fingerprint, and cannot name the infra cause (`crash`, `browser-unavailable`, `install`, `errors`) that tells Budi what to fix. The contract surfaces causes through `e2e_blocked_causes`, which this slice defers without naming a replacement.
implementation_impact: Whoever writes the docs has to tell the model either to parse the `.jsonl` histories by hand, which is the kind of hand-assembled verdict SKILL.md forbids, or to use the plan's `fail` reason as an approximation that ignores session. The infra-retry prompt cannot name the cause.
suggestion: Add per-cell output for the orchestrator. Options: (a) Runner output line `appended` entries as `{cell, state, reason}`; or (b) plan `layers.e2e[<b>]` gains `record_reason` and `record_session` for the newest record. Then rewrite both interim conditions in terms of that field.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1: 'run `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --cells V:<scoped browsers joined by +>`' vs Fase 2: 'group the scoped e2e entries ... into one `--cells <ver>:<b>[+<b>],…`')
issue: Fase 1 drives 'scoped browsers', meaning every browser in the run scope. Fase 2 drives 'scoped e2e entries', meaning only cells with a rerun entry. When V already has a fresh passing gate-grade cell (resumed session, or one cell failed on infra while the other passed), Fase 1 re-proves the passing cell and Fase 2 does not. The infra retry ('one more run on the same fingerprint') doesn't say which of the two sets it uses either.
implementation_impact: The docs could tell the model to boot browsers that are already proven, or to skip them. Each choice changes run time and which records exist.
suggestion: Use one definition for both phases. The likely intent is `--cells V:<browsers of V's scoped e2e rerun_matrix entries>`, with the infra retry limited to the cells whose newest record has an infra cause.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration ('E2E loop ended ... an E2E run printed `skipped` or exited 2') vs SKILL.md 'Vonis dan output' ('Exit 2 dari skrip manapun = error input: baca stderr, perbaiki, ulangi')
issue: The interim rule ends the E2E loop for the whole session on any exit 2 from an E2E run. SKILL.md's general rule says exit 2 is an input error: fix it and repeat. A typo in `--cells`, a malformed `--session`, or a cell outside the configured set therefore ends E2E for the session instead of being corrected. The docs task doesn't say whether the SKILL.md rule gets an E2E exception. The contract's 'E2E loop ended' list does not include exit 2.
implementation_impact: The SKILL.md text will contradict itself unless the writer picks a winner. Under the interim rule, one orchestrator mistake costs the session its E2E proof.
suggestion: Limit the rule to a child exit 2, recognisable by an output line with `ran` and exit 2, which means the child rejected its input. Treat a pre-spawn input error (no output line) as 'fix and repeat' per SKILL.md. Or keep the rule and add the E2E exception to the SKILL.md docs task explicitly.

location: Design Notes > Plan shape ('`rerun_matrix` stays a `--per-version` output; its e2e entries add `browser` and `reason`') / ps-plan-layers.py `PER_VERSION_LAYERS` + `per_version_rollup` (`per_version_capable`)
issue: Today every `rerun_matrix` entry carries `per_version_capable: layer in PER_VERSION_LAYERS`. `PER_VERSION_LAYERS` includes `e2e`, and the docstring says ps-run-layer runs e2e per version. In this slice, `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --per-version` is exit 2, and e2e entries now cover cells outside `--versions`. The spec doesn't say whether e2e entries keep `per_version_capable: true`, drop the key, or set it false. It also doesn't say whether `e2e` leaves `PER_VERSION_LAYERS`, which `plan_per_version` and `per_version_path` also use.
implementation_impact: If e2e entries keep `per_version_capable: true`, the orchestrator is invited to run the forbidden `--per-version` e2e command. Changing the constant without guidance could break the Layer 1/2/5 per-version planning that shares it.
suggestion: State that e2e `rerun_matrix` entries carry `per_version_capable: false` (or no such key), that `e2e` is removed from `PER_VERSION_LAYERS` along with any per-version e2e file planning, and update the docstrings to say so.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration ('Lapis 4 visual review (interactive, as today)') vs tier-matrix.md > Rules > Visual review (`visual-pending.json`, merge only after the current Phase 2's Layer 3 merge, drop entries of another session/fingerprint)
issue: The contract delays visual writes into `<module>-adversarial.json` until after Phase 2's Layer 3 merge, keeping them in `visual-pending.json` tagged with session and `source_fingerprint`. That rule is what stops a pre-patch visual defect from surviving the patch that fixed it, and stops a visual write from making stale Layer 3 output look fresh. The slice runs E2E (with screenshots) inside every Fase 1 iteration. It defers the pending mechanism without saying when a blocking visual defect may be written. 'As today' gives no timing: SKILL.md only says 'sebelum agregat jalan'.
implementation_impact: If the docs say 'write after each run', a visual finding from iteration N stays blocking in adversarial.json after the patch in iteration N+1 fixes it, and only a manual edit removes it. If the docs say 'write at the end', it's unclear which run's screenshots count.
suggestion: Add an interim rule. For example: review screenshots only of the last E2E run per version on the final fingerprint, and write blocking visual defects (read-merge) only after Fase 2's Layer 3 merge, just before the wrap-up. Alternatively, pull the `visual-pending.json` rule into this slice as written.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2: 'Then Layer 3 as today, spawned again after every loop-back unless the plan reuses it' and the wrap-up list)
issue: Three gaps here. (1) The only plan call in Fase 2 is `--per-version`, and the spec itself says per-version `rerun` always holds `adversarial`, because the per-version adversarial file never exists. So 'unless the plan reuses it' can never be true, and no field is named that would show Layer 3 reuse. (2) The wrap-up list (merge-only 2/5, e2e view, aggregate) leaves out the Layer 3 merge and the cross-version Layer 1 canonical scan that `ps-aggregate` needs (`<module>-static.json`). The contract's wrap-up includes both. (3) 'today's `--merge-only` for Layers 2 and 5' still needs `--versions`, and the spec doesn't say whether that is the in-scope versions or all configured versions.
implementation_impact: Whoever writes the docs has to guess when Layer 3 may be skipped and what the wrap-up order is. Leaving out the static scan can make the aggregate exit 2 (no static file) or read a stale one.
suggestion: Say that Layer 3 is always spawned in Fase 2, or name the canonical plan field that decides reuse. List the full wrap-up order: Layer 3 merge, cross-version static scan, `--merge-only` 2/5 with `--versions <all configured>`, e2e view, aggregate.

location: Design Notes > Record ('Version-level child fields (`run_id`, `boot`, `boot_id`, `boot_phases`, `boot_wall_clock`, `image_tag`, `errors`, `install`, `scenario_notes`) go into every record of that version') vs Boundaries > Always (`ps-e2e-run.py`: '`browser_mode`=`sequential`, `scenario_set`=`full`') and cell-contract.md > Producers (child emits `browser_mode` per version)
issue: The contract's Producers puts `browser_mode` at version level. The spec's version-level copy list leaves it out, and doesn't say whether the child emits `browser_mode` and `scenario_set` per version or per cell. So for `browser-unavailable` records (usable child output), and for cells where boot failed, it's unclear whether these fields are copied or `null`.
implementation_impact: The child's output shape and ps-run-layer's merge could be implemented differently, and the shape tests would encode whichever guess was made. It doesn't change the gate, since those records are inconclusive, but it is exactly the kind of detail test fixtures need.
suggestion: Add `browser_mode` to the version-level list. Say that `scenario_set` is per cell and is `null` on records where no engine started.

location: Boundaries > Never (`parallel browsers ... snapshot-db (CAP-7)`) vs cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Slots (the sequential fallback resets to the snapshot before each later engine) and SPEC.md CAP-6 (`snapshot-db` when the boot drives more than one browser)
issue: This slice's two-browser boots record `browser_mode: sequential` and count as gate-grade. Today the browsers share one DB with no reset. In the contract, `sequential` means each later engine starts from a reset snapshot. Once CAP-7 lands, readers can't tell this slice's non-isolated sequential records from contract sequential records, and both keep standing as gate-grade evidence.
implementation_impact: Evidence collected under weaker isolation will silently satisfy a later gate whose guarantee (each engine starts from the same state) it never had.
suggestion: Either accept this explicitly in Design Notes (sequential records from this slice remain gate-grade after CAP-7), or have this slice stamp a distinguishing value, e.g. `browser_mode: sequential-shared`, that CAP-7's gate-grade rule can exclude.

location: Design Notes > Runner interim ('ps-run-layer reads `--config` through its own key map ...: configured set, `psm_flashlight_tag_map`, `psm_flashlight_startup_timeout`')
issue: `psm_flashlight_startup_timeout` exists in the contract only to bound `wait-slots`, which this slice defers. The spec has ps-run-layer read it but gives it no use. It's unclear whether it should only be validated (exit 2 on a non-integer, per Config keys) or ignored.
implementation_impact: Either dead code or an untested validation path. The tests won't know whether a malformed value must give exit 2 in this slice.
suggestion: Drop it from this slice's key map, or say 'validated (exit 2 when it does not parse as an integer), otherwise unused'.

location: Design Notes > Runner interim ('a child reaped with returncode 143 or −15 counts as stopped, never `crash`')
issue: The rule covers a child that returns 143 or −15 while ps-run-layer itself was stopped. It doesn't cover a child that is SIGTERMed on its own (for example, `--stop-job` aimed at a different job whose PID matched, or an external kill) while ps-run-layer keeps running. In that case: are its cells appended as nothing, does ps-run-layer keep starting queued children, and what are its exit code and output line?
implementation_impact: The reap loop needs a branch whose behaviour isn't specified. Writing nothing and exiting 0 or 1 would lose the information that a version never ran.
suggestion: Say that a child stop without a ps-run-layer stop appends nothing for that child, continues the queue, leaves the cells out of `appended`, and gives exit 1 (or decide that such a child counts as `crash`).

location: Tasks > docs ('adversarial-lens.md (`--session` on plan calls; Layer 3 spawned again after a loop-back)')
issue: references/adversarial-lens.md contains no `ps-plan-layers.py` invocation, only a prose mention at line 132, so there is no plan call to add `--session` to. 'Loop-back' is a CAP-1 term; the interim equivalent is 'an appended fail re-enters Fase 1, then Fase 2 restarts'.
implementation_impact: The docs writer will either invent a plan command in adversarial-lens.md or skip the item, with no way of knowing which was intended.
suggestion: Reword the item: 'adversarial-lens.md: Layer 3 is spawned again whenever Fase 2 restarts after an E2E fail re-entered Fase 1 (no plan command lives there)'. Or drop the `--session` part.
